author: Kat Wong
description:
Body of a man in his 20s discovered by police who were sent to investigate the shooting of an officer, who is in a serious but stable condition

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

An on-duty police officer has been shot and a man found dead nearby as police investigate two firearm incidents in a tiny Tasmanian town.

The officer was working at Whitemark police station on Flinders Island, north-east of the island of Tasmania, when he was shot at about 9.45pm on Saturday night.

Continue reading...
title: Man found dead on Flinders Island linked to shooting of police officer, Tasmanian authorities say

author: Andrew Messenger
description:
A government in office for more than two years is finally forced to take responsibility and seemingly no longer able to blame its Labor predecessors

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

At the beginning of another Queensland parliamentary sitting week, anonymous sources were out in force, this time background briefing against the state’s Labor leader, Steven Miles.

It is no great revelation to observers of Queensland politics that Miles, still seemingly bruised from his election loss two years ago, has struggled to find his feet as opposition leader. Many wondered why he wanted to stay on after the party’s drubbing in 2024. Some of Labor’s factional whisperers were telling anyone who would listen that the former premier
title: ‘Six, seven, maybe more preventable deaths’: Queensland’s LNP faces reckoning over broken health system

author: Melissa Davey Medical editor
description:
Copini Beauty referred to New South Wales health regulators, while federal government says it is ‘deeply concerned’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

An Australian beauty company that promotes “clean” ingredients “free from skin irritants” has been referred to state health regulators after appearing to offer cigarettes to guests at a beachside lip gloss launch.

Photos from an event held earlier in November at a venue in Bondi, Sydney show what appears to be loose cigarettes without health warnings on a tiered silver platter alongside a bowl of lip glosses.

Continue reading...</
title: Cigarettes on silver platters at Bondi ‘clean’ beauty business lip gloss launch referred for investigation

author: Tory Shepherd
description:
GiveSendGo has been accused of facilitating the financing of extremism, but the platform says it does not ‘condone racism, discrimination, hate speech, or violence of any kind’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australian neo-Nazis have raised hundreds of thousands of dollars on the global crowdfunding platform GiveSendGo, which has been accused of facilitating the financing of hate and extremism.

Of the 68 Australian fundraisers on the site, the White Australia party has raised the fourth-highest amount of money with $200,000 for its high court battle to overturn its
title: Australian neo-Nazis among far-right groups raising hundreds of thousands via global crowdfunding platform

author: Keely Aouga
description:
Jared Schurr arrested in Mississippi after Lizeht Rodriguez and Woodrow Scott died in otherwise unrelated killings

A man recently strangled a woman to death whom he did not know along a hiking trail north of New Orleans – then killed his co-worker with a crossbow two days later before being arrested in Mississippi after a police chase, authorities allege.

Jared Schurr, 36, faces counts of second-degree murder in the killings of Lizeht Rodriguez, 24, and Woodrow Scott, 37, on 11 and 13 November, respectively, investigators said on Saturday.

Continue reading...
title: Louisiana man charged with killing woman on hiking trail and murdering co-worker with crossbow

author: Harry Cockburn
description:
Local MP says legitimate criticisms of asylum housing plans are being co-opted by opposition parties ‘stirring up racial discord’

Residents of a Suffolk village have voted to “leave the UK” in a referendum held in response to government plans to house 930 asylum seekers at a nearby former military base.

Approximately 500 people in Barnham were eligible to take part in the symbolic vote on Saturday. There were 257 votes for independence, 16 against and one spoiled ballot.

Continue reading...
title: Suffolk village votes to ‘leave the UK’ over plans to house asylum seekers nearby

author: Associated Press
description:
Anticipating flood of Democratic requests, US president issues executive order in attempt to stymie oversight efforts

Donald Trump is directing federal contractors and subcontractors to consult with his administration about inquiries they receive from Congress and to withhold any communications that the White House considers privileged, according to an executive order issued late Friday.

The companies must also coordinate with the White House and US agencies on “appropriate responses” to any such requests, the order says. If they fail to comply, the White House warns, their contracts could be terminated and their future work with the federal government suspended.

Continue reading...
title: Trump orders contractors to check with White House over any congressional inquiries

author: Robert Mackey
description:
US vice-president says it’s not his place to second-guess the president, but refrains from endorsing Trump’s claim

At a White House news conference on Friday, JD Vance stopped short of endorsing Donald Trump’s claim that Iran was so close to obtaining a nuclear weapon in February that it was essential for the US to go to war with the Islamic republic.

In the White House briefing room, Trump was asked about reporting this week that he was unhappy with the US vice-president’s statement blaming Republican losses in the midterm elections on the Iran war.

Continue reading...
title: Vance stops short of endorsing Trump’s claim that Iran was close to nuclear weapon

author: José Olivares
description:
Levent Alpöge says it took six weeks for him using the AI tool to solve the math problem involving prime numbers

A mathematician at Anthropic is contending that the San Francisco-based artificial intelligence (AI) company’s software has helped crack one of the most important unsolved problems in mathematics.

Levent Alpöge, a Turkish American mathematician, on Friday posted a note on his personal website saying that Claude, the AI software, had helped prove the Riemann hypothesis. He says that Claude helped develop a solution to the problem during the course of about six weeks.

Continue reading...
title: Anthropic mathematician claims he used Claude to prove 19th-century Riemann hypothesis

author: Associated Press
description:
Oscar Belgal, a Dominican national, was shot by ICE agents as he drove his five-year-old son home from school

A federal judge on Friday declined to release from custody a man who was shot and wounded by immigration officers as they arrested him in New York in October.

The US district court judge Hector Gonzalez said in a written ruling that agents may have made a procedural error in serving an arrest warrant on Oscar Belgal before he was given a notice to appear in immigration court. However, he wrote, that was merely a technical error that does not require Belgal to be released from federal custody pending deportation proceedings.

Continue reading...
title: Federal judge denies request to release man shot by immigration agents in New York

author: Sara Sneath in Miami
description:
Temperatures in a concrete facility contributed to one man’s death after he struggled to breathe, prisoners allege

On Tuesday afternoon Dwayne Wilson, 69, a thin Black man dressed in a light gray prison uniform, testified about the stifling heat he experienced in the Dade correctional institute, a concrete state prison south of Miami, Florida, without air conditioning. He removed his glasses and wiped his eyes as he spoke. “It was so hot,” he said, his voice catching. “It’s so hot sometimes you have to put water on the floor just to try to keep cool.”

Wilson said he’s housed in the H dorms, a T-shaped building with one-to-two-person cells, nicknamed “hell dorm” by prisoners because its concrete walls radiate heat absorbed from the sun. The plaintiff’s law firm, the Florida Justice Institute
title: ‘Hell dorm’: Florida prisoners testify about 119F heat indexes and walls that sweat

author: Alice Speri
description:
Chris Van Hollen and Chuck Schumer represent conflicting visions on issue that has become ‘litmus test’ for Democratic voters

The race to lead the Democratic Party’s incoming Senate majority has become the latest battlefield between two conflicting visions for how the US should relate to Israel – a once unquestioned ally whose collapsing standing among the US public has become a defining feature of American politics.

Chuck Schumer, the veteran New York Senator and current Democratic minority leader, is one of Israel’s most reliable supporters in Congress. As he views it, according to an interview he gave last year, his “job” is to “keep the left pro-Israel”.
title: Race to lead Senate Democrats the latest battlefield in party’s tussle over Israel

author: David Hammer of WWL Louisiana and Ramon Antonio Vargas in New Orleans
description:
Arrival of payments in contentious legal saga that began in 2020 is ‘a weight off my shoulders’, one survivor said

Hundreds of clergy sexual abuse survivors have received more than half of the $305m bankruptcy settlement that the archdiocese of New Orleans reached with them last year, a milestone that marks the beginning of the end of a years-long legal saga.

The trustee overseeing the settlement fund, Don Massey, confirmed on Friday that $180m had been distributed to 450 of about 740 survivors, either directly or through their lawyers if they retained legal representation. Massey said he and his staff are working hard to get payments in the rest of the survivors’ hands by the end of the year but are still waiting on hundreds of distribution forms from survivors and their lawyers.
title: New Orleans Catholic clergy abuse survivors begin receiving payments from $305m bankruptcy settlement

author: Fiona Harvey in Antalya
description:
Exclusive: Countries at Cop31 are being urged to commit to deriving 35% of their energy from electricity by 2035

  • Cop31 live – latest updates

China is pushing for rapid electrification of its economy using low-carbon energy and will help other countries do the same, a senior member of the Chinese delegation at the Cop31 UN climate summit has said.

Wang Yi, a professor of energy and environment policy at the Chinese Academy of Sciences and a senior adviser to China’s government, said: “End-use electrification is a very clear direction. We can follow this direction while making the source of electricity clean. That’s the way to go forward.”
title: China commits to low-carbon electrification and help for others to improve

author: Emine Sinmaz and Alexandra Topping
description:
Experts say no law states third-party consent is a valid defence and call for public debate and further education

Campaigners have welcomed a call for scrutiny of consent laws by a survivor of drug-facilitated rape but said action must also focus on wider issues around sexual assault.

Joanne Young, who was drugged and raped by her husband and sexually abused by men he invited into their home, warned of “serious questions about how the law deals with consent”.

Continue reading...
title: Campaigners back call for scrutiny of consent laws by Joanne Young

author: Nino Bucci
description:
Victoria police say boy, 17, communicated with offenders under username ‘Onepercent’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Victorian police allege a 17-year-old boy tasked others to carry out a series of arsons, home invasions and a mistaken identity kidnapping that resulted in the partial amputation of a victim’s finger during Melbourne’s hospitality wars.

The boy, who was arrested on Friday afternoon, allegedly communicated with the offenders under the username “Onepercent” on the encrypted communications app Signal.

Continue reading...
title: Teenager allegedly organised arsons and kidnapping on Signal during Melbourne hospitality wars

author: Henry Belot
description:
Exclusive: Independent candidate Tosh-Jake Finnigan’s cards instruct people to vote in a way that would benefit Liberal party

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

The Victorian Greens are seeking an urgent injunction from the supreme court to stop an independent candidate distributing how-to-vote cards that allegedly mimic the party’s branding and urge people to preference it last.

As prepoll opened on Wednesday morning, Tosh-Jake Finnigan’s campaign team handed out how-to-vote cards that used the minor party’s colour scheme, font and triangle logo with the banner “Vote 1 Green Values”.
title: Victorian Greens seek urgent injunction over how-to-vote cards mimicking party’s branding but preferencing it last

author: David Smith in Washington
description:
The president appeared to put Vance and Rubio through their paces as potential successors, though Stephen Miller unexpectedly stole the spotlight

“Which of you shall we say doth love us most?”

The ageing King Lear’s question to his daughters, expecting them to compete for his favour and carve up his kingdom, hovered in the White House press briefing room on Friday.

Continue reading...
title: Trump turns White House press conference into a 2028 succession audition
